data.narrative:
Elroy Air, a Series B drone and autonomous systems company founded by David Merrill and Clint Cope, carries a current post-money valuation of $800M against $116M raised to date. The valuation exercise draws from a sector comprising 8 private peers including Zipline, Joby Aviation, Nuro, Archer Aviation, and Manna Aero, with no public comparables available in the narrow drones and autonomous subsector.

Peer-median analysis proved inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage datapoints within the narrow peer universe; a broader sector median would introduce unacceptable noise. Stage-progression methodology is applicable and drives the primary valuation signal. Applying a 1.9x multiplier—the typical step-up from Series B to subsequent funding—to the $800M last post-money valuation yields $1.52B.

The analysis supports a triangulated valuation range of $1.3B (low) to $1.7B (high), with a central estimate of $1.5B. This narrow 30% band reflects reliance on a single methodological anchor. Key uncertainties include the limited depth of same-stage comparable financials in frontier drone markets, continued regulatory clarity around autonomous operations, and unit economics demonstration in near-term revenue milestones. Any material shift in comparable valuations or sector funding momentum would warrant recalibration.
